title: Cubism
statementMd:
Magikarp is trying out a new technique called *Cubism*. With a carefully arranged set of blocks, he can create three different images when viewed from different angles!

Magikarp has a grid of n×m×k positions, measured along the x-, y-, and z-axes, respectively. Each position (x,y,z), where 1≤x≤n, 1≤y≤m, and 1≤z≤k, can contain at most one unit cube. Cubes may float freely and do not need to be connected.

When standing in front of the sculpture, +x points to your right, +y points forward into the sculpture, and +z points upward. Each view is an orthogonal projection: its lines of sight are parallel to its viewing direction.

He has already chosen three images for his artwork:

- The **top view** looks in the −z direction, with +x to the right and +y upward in the image. It has m rows and n columns.
- The **front view** looks in the +y direction, with +x to the right and +z upward in the image. It has k rows and n columns.
- The **right view** looks in the −x direction, with +y to the right and +z upward in the image. It has k rows and m columns.

An entry is `#` if at least one cube exists along its line of sight, and `.` if no cube exists along that line.

Find the maximum number of cubes Magikarp can place so that all three views match his chosen images exactly. If no such arrangement exists, output `-1`.

## Input

The first line contains three integers n, m, and k (1≤n,m,k≤300) — the numbers of positions along the x-, y-, and z-axes, respectively.

The next m lines each contain a string of n characters — the top view.

The next k lines each contain a string of n characters — the front view.

The next k lines each contain a string of m characters — the right view.

Each character is either `#` or `.`. Each image is given row by row from top to bottom, with each row written from left to right, using the orientations defined above.

## Output

Output a single integer — the maximum number of cubes in an arrangement matching all three views, or `-1` if no such arrangement exists.

## Note

In the first sample, all eight positions can contain cubes.

In the second sample, the front and top views spell "KARP" and "CARP", respectively. A maximum of 139 cube positions can be filled.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d0042aa57ed984aaca7f7eba7070e769e7508790.png) Second sample: front view ("KARP"). ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3aaab4bc51d5fe8a3119fa219d51380bbb70321c.png) Second sample: top view ("CARP"). ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4e5b93bc265c4d1b874377255090a89c37969d8a.png) Second sample: filled right view.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/093a4a4439c87369be37ebef466942695349df3f.png) Close-up of the sculpture in the second sample, or see a video [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1928GSQBgi-tlPVWP9pqPgBD7HcLAqbHt/view?usp=sharing).

In the third sample, the top view requires a cube with x=1 and y=1. The front view allows such a cube only at z=1, but the right view forbids a cube with y=1 and z=1. Therefore, no arrangement exists.
